offspring.title: Trajectory-cost evaluation protocol with matched budgets and rank-reversal test
offspring.method: Starting from the probe (C02) and the oracle (C01), define the evaluation that any step-wise method must pass before a claim is made. (1) Cost accounting: U(lambda) = Acc - lambda*sum_t c_{k(t)}; charge probe/estimator overhead, branching/label-generation cost and any extra tokens in a single 'compute' column. (2) Metrics: U-AUC over a fixed lambda grid, calls per trajectory, per-step unnecessary and missed-necessary rates, flip rate. (3) Matched budgets: all methods are compared at equal numbers of tool calls (interpolated U-vs-calls curves) and at equal added tokens. (4) Rank-reversal test: compare method rankings under the anchor's single-call TR metric (applied to 'any call in the trajectory') versus cumulative per-trajectory cost.
offspring.experiment: Methods: never/always, anchor-style explicit-confidence threshold (reduced), Probe&Prefill (single pre-generation), SeaKR/FLARE-style step triggers, step-wise need-probe, our utility probe. Benchmarks as in C01. Measure Kendall tau between method rankings under the two cost definitions, bootstrapped over instances.
offspring.diff_vs_parents: Moves from an estimator or a measurement to the evaluation protocol: a different contribution aimed at the prompt's requirement to distinguish single-call TR from cumulative cost.
offspring.hypothesis: On multi-call benchmarks the ranking of methods by U-AUC under cumulative per-trajectory cost differs from the ranking under the single-call 'any call' tool-rate (Kendall tau < 1 with bootstrap 95% CI excluding 1) for at least one benchmark.
offspring.novelty_note: Low-moderate: a protocol contribution; supports every other idea; not claimed as a method.

offspring.title: Look-ahead probing: probe the hidden state after a cheap draft of the next step
offspring.method: Assumption challenged in C02: the decision must be made from the state BEFORE the step is written. Alternative: generate a short draft of the next step (up to d tokens, discarded if a call is chosen), take the hidden state at the end of the draft and apply the two-head probe. The draft reveals what the model is about to do (e.g. an arithmetic expression it is unsure about), information not in the pre-step state. Draft tokens are charged in compute.
offspring.experiment: Pre-step vs look-ahead probes at d in {8, 16, 32}; metric Delta-sign AUROC, U-AUC, and net U after charging draft tokens at the benchmark's token price ratio r in {0, 0.01, 0.05} of a tool call.
offspring.diff_vs_parents: Changes the probe's INPUT TIMING (pre-step -> post-draft) rather than the label or decision rule; conceptually related to FLARE's forward-looking sentence but with hidden-state probes and utility labels.
offspring.hypothesis: Look-ahead probes improve per-step Delta-sign AUROC by at least 0.05 over pre-step probes at d = 16, and their net U-AUC exceeds pre-step probes only when the draft cost ratio r is below a break-even value reported with a CI.
offspring.novelty_note: FLARE (E21) anticipates the next sentence to decide retrieval from token probabilities; hidden-state utility probes after a draft are not in the matrix.

offspring.compatibility_check: G1b's flip labels are computed from C01's branched Delta labels and share the same data and estimator for Delta; the combination is an attribution of oracle headroom to flip steps. COMPATIBLE.
offspring.title: Noise-corrected headroom attribution to decision-flip steps
offspring.method: Crossover: report the oracle headroom of C01 decomposed over flip steps (G1b) versus non-flip steps. Mutation (fix weakest shared criticism: both depend on noisy K=3 Delta labels): keep a flip or a headroom contribution only if the sign of Delta_t - lambda*c agrees between two independent halves of the branch samples (split-half reliability), and report headroom under the reliable-flip filter with a permutation null where Delta labels are shuffled within instance.
offspring.experiment: Headroom (U-AUC gap) with and without the reliability filter; share of the gap carried by reliable flips; permutation-null distribution of the gap.
offspring.diff_vs_parents: Adds the decomposition (G1b) to C01's headroom estimate and a reliability filter + permutation null (mutation) so noise cannot masquerade as headroom.
offspring.hypothesis: After restricting to split-half-reliable flip steps, at least half of the measured oracle headroom persists and exceeds the 95th percentile of the permutation-null gap; otherwise the apparent headroom is attributed to label noise.
offspring.novelty_note: Methodological rigour added to C01/G1b; honest about winner's-curse bias.

offspring.title: Benefit-ranked risk-controlled skipping
offspring.method: Weakest criticism of C06: the guarantee may force always-call, so savings depend on the score that ranks queries for skipping. Change ONE component, the ranking score: rank candidate-skip queries by estimated benefit Delta_hat (call benefit minus cost) from a calibrated estimator instead of by direct-answer confidence; the Learn-then-Test calibration of the skip threshold on the accuracy-loss risk is unchanged.
offspring.experiment: Calls saved at epsilon in {1,2,5}% with confidence-ranked vs benefit-ranked skipping over 20 random calibration/test splits; empirical risk <= epsilon rate.
offspring.diff_vs_parents: Only the ranking score changes (direct confidence -> estimated benefit).
offspring.hypothesis: At epsilon = 5%, benefit-ranked skipping saves a larger fraction of calls than confidence-ranked skipping (paired across splits, 95% CI excluding 0) while the risk guarantee holds in at least 1-delta of splits for both.
offspring.novelty_note: Depends on a benefit estimator; inherits the E12 risk.

offspring.operator: CROSSOVER-COMBINATION (EMPTY) -> parent copy of P2-G1b, then MUTATION-TARGETED
offspring.compatibility_check: G1b already contains C01's per-query p_tool; there is no complementary mechanism in C01 to add. Crossover returns EMPTY; per HypoEvolve's rule the offspring is an unchanged copy of G1b, to which the planned mutation applies.
offspring.title: Failure-aware two-sided estimator with a tool-preview signal
offspring.method: Weakest criticism of G1b (inherited E12 risk): query-text features may not predict tool success beyond a constant. Change ONE component, the p_tool signal: add cheap tool-preview features (retrieval top-k score statistics and title overlap for the retrieval scenario; expression size and parse depth for the calculator; classifier output for the reasoner) to the p_tool_hat features, charging the preview cost. Remainder of G1b unchanged.
offspring.experiment: p_tool AUROC and net U with query-only vs query+preview features per scenario; preview cost sensitivity.
offspring.diff_vs_parents: Single change: p_tool features gain a tool-preview signal. Reintroduces the preview signal of an eliminated candidate (P2-C02) as a targeted fix.
offspring.hypothesis: On the retrieval scenario, adding preview features raises p_tool AUROC by at least 0.05 over query-only features and increases net U-AUC after charging preview cost; no gain is expected on the calculator scenario.
offspring.novelty_note: Preview-based value-of-information for tool benefit not found; narrow scope.

offspring.compatibility_check: G1c's stage 1 uses unspecified direct-side signals; G1b's failure-aware direct estimator is exactly such a signal. Complementary, no conflicting assumptions. COMPATIBLE.
offspring.title: Gated benefit estimation driven by a failure-aware direct signal
offspring.method: Stage 1 uses G1b's failure-aware p_direct (consensus + verbalized + confidently-wrong correction) as the gating signal: clear-high answer directly, clear-low call; stage 2 (only in the uncertain band) consults the per-query p_tool_hat. Gate thresholds tuned jointly with the correction on the shared validation split by net U.
offspring.experiment: Gate rate, U-AUC and signal cost vs G1b (always two-sided), G1c (gate on plain direct signals), CTA global rule, direct-only.
offspring.diff_vs_parents: Replaces G1c's plain direct-side signal with G1b's failure-aware estimate and tunes the gate with it; gates G1b's p_tool consultation.
offspring.hypothesis: The merged rule matches G1b's U-AUC within 1 point while consulting p_tool_hat for fewer than 40% of queries, and has a lower confidently-wrong skip rate than G1c's gate on plain signals.
offspring.novelty_note: Close to G1b/G1c; distinctiveness against them will be scored low.
